target: Пусть идёт дождь, мы всё равно пойдём.
english: Let it rain, we will go anyway.
grammar: Пусть + 3rd person = concessive 'let/even if': Пусть идёт дождь = Let it rain. Всё равно = anyway/regardless.

target: Где бы ты ни был, я найду тебя.
english: Wherever you are, I will find you.

target: До тех пор пока не будет ответа, мы ждём.
english: Until there is an answer, we wait.
For the sake of the children she tries.
She got up, got dressed, and went out.
After lunch we will go for a walk.
According to the plan, we will start tomorrow.
In the city center there are many stores.
grammar: В центре + genitive = in the center of: в центре города. Много + genitive plural: много магазинов = many stores.

english: For the sake of health he quit smoking.

target: Как только он придёт, мы начнём.
english: As soon as he arrives, we will begin.
grammar: Как только = 'as soon as': Как только он придёт, мы начнём. A temporal conjunction for immediate sequence of events.

target: Мы пойдём, если только не будет грозы.
english: We will go unless there is a thunderstorm.
grammar: Если только не = 'unless': мы пойдём, если только не будет грозы. Conditional with exception.

target: Письмо было отправлено вчера утром по почте.
english: The letter was sent yesterday morning by mail.
grammar: Не в своей тарелке (not in one's plate) means feeling uncomfortable or out of place.

target: Все билеты были проданы за два часа.
english: All tickets were sold out in two hours.
At the beginning of the lesson the teacher explained.

target: Скоро писатель слушает музыку в магазине.
english: Soon the writer listens to music in the store.
grammar: Скоро (soon) + present tense for near-future planned events. Слушать музыку = to listen to music. В магазине = in the store.

english: On the edge of the forest stands a little house.
grammar: На + accusative for direction: на работу (to work). На + prepositional for location: на работе (at work).

target: Играющие во дворе дети шумели до самого вечера.
english: The children playing in the yard were noisy until evening.
grammar: Short form passive participles: прочитан, написана, сделано, открыты.

target: Закрытый магазин откроется завтра утром в девять часов.
english: The closed store will open tomorrow morning at nine o'clock.

target: Физик продемонстрировал новую теорию гравитации на конференции.
english: The physicist demonstrated a new theory of gravitation at the conference.
grammar: Не только...но и means 'not only...but also': Не только красивый, но и умный.

target: Пивовар варил тёмное пиво по старинному монастырскому рецепту.
english: The brewer brewed dark beer according to an old monastery recipe.
grammar: Compound numbers: двадцать один (21) takes nominative, двадцать два (22) takes genitive singular.

target: Мельник молол зерно на старой ветряной мельнице у реки.
english: The miller ground grain at the old windmill by the river.
grammar: Ходить implies repeated trips: Я хожу в школу (I go to school regularly).

target: Нам пора идти, автобус отходит через пять минут.
english: It's time for us to go, the bus leaves in five minutes.

target: Слушая лекцию, она аккуратно записывала заметки в новую тетрадь.
english: While listening to the lecture, she took careful notes in her new notebook.

target: Сломанный велосипед был починен моим отцом менее чем за час.
english: The broken bicycle was fixed by my father in less than an hour.

target: Покрашенный забор вокруг сада придаёт всему дому свежий вид.
english: The painted fence around the garden gives the whole house a fresh new look.

target: Решённая задача помогла команде двигаться дальше с остальной частью проекта.
english: The solved problem helped the team move forward with the rest of the project.
She misses home.
Regarding your question.
She is from Russia.
It's boring without you.
A gift for mom.
He rarely is late.
grammar: Редко (rarely) + inverted word order: Редко он опаздывает. Placing the adverb first emphasizes infrequency.

english: She lives with mom.
grammar: Однако means 'however': Однако, это не совсем так (However, this is not quite so).

english: Before bed I read.
I came from abroad.
Despite difficulties, he managed.
She read quickly a task.
grammar: Учить (impf.) vs выучить (pf.) — studying vs having learned.

english: She is going to work.
I am thinking about work.
grammar: Думать о + prepositional = to think about: думаю о работе. О + prepositional for the topic of thought.

english: He is talking about Russia.
This is important for me.
We walked through the park.
grammar: Через + accusative = 'through/across': прошли через парк. Пройти is perfective of проходить — we walked through.

english: She hid behind a tree.
grammar: Тем не менее means 'nevertheless': Тем не менее, он продолжал работать.

english: He walks around the park.
He sits across from me.
grammar: Напротив + genitive = 'opposite/across from': напротив меня. Сидит = is sitting (position verb).

english: Sometimes I get up early.
Meanwhile the children were playing.
He told us the news.
During the day he worked.
She walks next to me.
Along with work he studies.
They always help each other.
Three years ago we met.
Hi, you look great today!
The cat is under the table.
The book being read is interesting.
I am sitting by the window.
He is waiting at the entrance.
grammar: У + genitive = 'at/near': у входа = at the entrance. Ждёт = is waiting (imperfective for ongoing action).

english: We will go along the road.
grammar: По + dative for route: по дороге = along the road. Поехать is perfective — we will go (by vehicle).

english: The cat jumped onto the couch.
The bird sat on a branch.
The ball rolled under the bed.
grammar: Под + accusative = motion under: закатился под кровать = rolled under the bed. Compare: под кроватью (under the bed, location).

english: On the occasion of the birthday.
The children ran around the yard.
grammar: Unidirectional: идти/ехать (going one way now). Multidirectional: ходить/ездить (going generally/repeatedly).

english: What time does the lesson start?
I will come in an hour.
He read all day a task.
She drove the children to school.
grammar: Prefix об- means 'around': обходить = to go around, объехать = to drive around.

english: We will arrive in two days.
Two days ago it was warm.
From time to time she calls.
This is my first time here.
grammar: Утром, днём, вечером, ночью — instrumental case for parts of day.

english: In childhood I loved ice cream.
They said that they don't know.
grammar: Прямая речь (direct speech) uses «»: Он сказал: «Я приду» = He said, 'I will come.'

english: They say winter will be cold.
I was told that you called.
Someone said that we are late.
grammar: Чтобы replaces imperative in reported speech: Он попросил, чтобы я пришёл.

english: Everyone knew that he was leaving.
grammar: Reported speech uses что: Он сказал, что придёт = He said that he would come.

target: Он работает с девяти до пяти.
english: He works from nine to five.

target: Почему ты не ответил на моё сообщение?
english: Why didn't you answer my message?
Between the houses there is a park.
Around the house there is a fence.
Along the river there is a path.
grammar: Вдоль + genitive = 'along': вдоль реки = along the river. Тропинка = footpath (feminine noun).

english: It's still too early to get up.
It's already too late for a walk.
Behind the house there is a garden.
She peeked out from behind the corner.
grammar: Из-за + genitive = 'from behind': выглянула из-за угла = peeked out from behind the corner. Compound preposition.

english: He will come no earlier than eight.
The children said they want ice cream.
grammar: Reported speech uses что: Он сказал, что придёт (He said that he would come).

english: The boss said the meeting is postponed.
The teacher demanded that everyone be quiet.
Having said goodbye to friends, we left.

target: Каждую неделю мы ходим в магазин.
english: Every week we go to the store.

target: Каждый месяц он платит за квартиру.
english: Every month he pays for the apartment.

target: В это время я обычно обедаю.
english: At this time I usually have lunch.

target: Мама велела, чтобы я убрал комнату.
english: Mom told me to clean the room.

target: Врач посоветовал, чтобы я больше отдыхал.
english: The doctor advised me to rest more.
grammar: Прямая речь (direct speech) uses «»: Он сказал: «Я приду» = He said, 'I will come.'

target: Эта книга читается с большим интересом.
english: This book is read with great interest.

target: На прошлой неделе мы были в театре.
english: Last week we were at the theater.

target: Ревность постепенно разрушила их многолетнюю крепкую дружбу.
english: Jealousy gradually destroyed their long-standing strong friendship.
The day after tomorrow it will be sunny.
I am standing in front of the house.
Half an hour ago it started to rain.
It is known that the Earth is round.
grammar: Чтобы replaces imperative in reported speech: Он попросил, чтобы я пришёл.

english: He pulled the box from under the bed.
grammar: Из-под + genitive = 'from under': из-под кровати = from under the bed. A compound preposition for extraction from beneath.

english: I was told that I need to wait.
grammar: Questions in reported speech use ли: Он спросил, придёт ли она.

english: Having learned the news, he called a friend.

target: Дети бегают во дворе после школы.
english: The children run around the yard after school.

target: Друг рассказал, что был в Париже.
english: A friend told that he was in Paris.

target: Заплатив за обед, мы вышли из ресторана.
english: Having paid for lunch, we left the restaurant.

target: Билеты на поезд забронированы на пятницу вечером.
english: Train tickets have been booked for Friday evening.

target: Не имея денег, он не мог купить билет.
english: Not having money, he couldn't buy a ticket.
grammar: Using ты with strangers or elders is considered rude — always start with Вы.

english: At the end of the street stands a church.
grammar: В конце + genitive = 'at the end of': в конце улицы. Стоит means 'stands' for buildings. Церковь = church (feminine).

target: Сначала он поел, потом пошёл гулять.
english: First he ate, then he went for a walk.
grammar: Prefixes change meaning: выходить (to go out), входить (to go in), уходить (to leave).

target: Ему передали, что собрание в три.
english: He was told that the meeting is at three.
grammar: Прямая речь (direct speech) uses «»: Он сказал: «Я приду» = He said, 'I will come.'

target: Как пройти до ближайшей станции метро?
english: How do I get to the nearest metro station?
grammar: Здравствуйте is formal; use Привет with friends.

target: Фехтовальщик отразил атаку соперника с великолепной точностью.
english: The fencer parried the opponent's attack with superb precision.
grammar: Отразить атаку = to parry/deflect an attack. С + instrumental: с великолепной точностью = with magnificent precision.

target: Акушерка сопровождала будущую мать на протяжении родов.
english: The midwife accompanied the expectant mother throughout the birth.
grammar: Утром, днём, вечером, ночью — instrumental case for parts of day.

target: Не поняв вопрос, она попросила повторить.
english: Not having understood the question, she asked to repeat it.

target: Археолог осторожно расчищал древнюю мозаику в раскопе.
english: The archaeologist carefully uncovered an ancient mosaic at the dig.

target: Сегодня понедельник, и впереди целая рабочая неделя.
english: Today is Monday, and a whole work week lies ahead.

target: Говоря по телефону, она ходила по комнате.
english: While talking on the phone, she walked around the room.
grammar: Gerunds don't change form — they are invariable verbal adverbs.

target: Хотя шёл дождь, мы всё равно пошли гулять.
english: Although it was raining, we went for a walk anyway.
grammar: The prepositional case is used after о, в, and на for location.

target: Доброе утро, хотите чашку чая или кофе?
english: Good morning, would you like a cup of tea or coffee?
grammar: Доброе утро = Good morning (formal greeting). Хотите = do you want (formal/plural). Чашку чая = a cup of tea (genitive after чашку).

target: Архитектор спроектировал современный культурный центр из стекла и стали.
english: The architect designed a modern cultural center of glass and steel.

target: Стекольщик вставил витражное стекло в окно старинной церкви.
english: The glazier installed stained glass in the window of the old church.
grammar: Носить/нести (to carry walking), возить/везти (to carry by vehicle) are also motion verbs.

target: Гуляя по старому району, они обнаружили очаровательный маленький книжный магазин.
english: While walking through the old district, they discovered a charming little bookshop.

target: Прощаясь в аэропорту, она не смогла сдержать слёзы.
english: While saying goodbye at the airport, she could not hold back her tears.
grammar: The gerund's subject must be the same as the main verb's subject.

target: Только что построенный дом на углу нашей улицы выглядит очень современно.
english: The newly built house on the corner of our street looks very modern.

target: Одетый ребёнок был готов идти в школу ещё до семи утра.
english: The dressed child was ready to leave for school before seven in the morning.

target: Плотно позавтракав, семья отправилась в путь на дачу.
english: Having eaten a hearty breakfast, the family set off on their journey to the dacha.

target: Свежий хлеб пекут каждое утро в маленькой пекарне на углу нашей улицы.
english: Fresh bread is baked every morning in the small bakery on the corner of our street.
We moved recently.
Time flies quickly.
Never say never.
Meanwhile night fell.
grammar: Утром, днём, вечером, ночью — instrumental case for parts of day.

english: She offered to help.
grammar: Спросить introduces reported questions: Она спросила, где я живу (She asked where I live).

english: The grown-up children left.
Time flies very fast.
The bird flew south.
grammar: Улететь means 'to fly away.' Prefix у- = departure. На юг = to the south (на + accusative for direction).

english: They say he left.
In winter we ski.
They drove around the city.
In spring the birds return.
grammar: Утром, днём, вечером, ночью — instrumental case for parts of day.

english: She was advised to rest.
grammar: Questions in reported speech use ли: Он спросил, придёт ли она.

english: The falling snow is beautiful.
The told story is interesting.
We drove past the park.
He ran away from class.
We ran across the road.
She flew across the ocean.
We walked the whole day.
grammar: Утром, днём, вечером, ночью — instrumental case for parts of day.

english: Mom asked to say hello.
grammar: Сказать/говорить (to say/tell) introduce direct and indirect speech.

english: They were told what happened.
grammar: Reported speech uses что: Он сказал, что придёт = He said that he would come.

english: Day after day he studied.
He asked where I live.
We drove around the traffic jam.
In autumn the leaves turn yellow.
The surprised eyes of the child.
The plane flew over the city.
She promised that she would call.
grammar: Прямая речь (direct speech) uses «»: Он сказал: «Я приду» = He said, 'I will come.'

english: He claimed that he was right.
He inquired where I am from.
The bored child wants to play.
On Thursday I have an exam.
grammar: В четверг = on Thursday (в + accusative for days of the week). У меня экзамен = I have an exam (у + genitive for possession).

english: With each day it gets warmer.
Once we went to the sea.
grammar: Однажды means 'once/one day' for past narrative. Поехали is past perfective plural — we went (by vehicle).

english: He asked how much it costs.
He asked not to disturb him.
Everyone said that he is talented.
grammar: Questions in reported speech use ли: Он спросил, придёт ли она.

english: She mentioned that she saw you.
grammar: Russian keeps the original tense in reported speech: Он сказал: 'Я приду' → Он сказал, что придёт.

target: Каждый день я хожу на работу.
english: Every day I go to work.

target: Каждый год мы ездим в отпуск.
english: Every year we go on vacation.
grammar: Утром, днём, вечером, ночью — instrumental case for parts of day.

target: На следующей неделе у нас праздник.
english: Next week we have a celebration.

target: Врач спросил, как я себя чувствую.
english: The doctor asked how I feel.
grammar: Чтобы replaces imperative in reported speech: Он попросил, чтобы я пришёл.

target: Он попросил, чтобы я помог ему.
english: He asked me to help him.
grammar: Questions in reported speech use ли: Он спросил, придёт ли она.

target: Он ответил, что не может прийти.
english: He answered that he cannot come.
grammar: Reported speech uses что: Он сказал, что придёт = He said that he would come.

target: Никто не сказал, что будет легко.
english: Nobody said it would be easy.
grammar: Прямая речь (direct speech) uses «»: Он сказал: «Я приду» = He said, 'I will come.'

target: В прошлом году я был в Париже.
english: Last year I was in Paris.
grammar: Пойти is perfective of идти: Я пошёл (I set off walking).

target: Из года в год мы приезжаем сюда.
english: Year after year we come here.
grammar: Сначала (first), потом (then), затем (after that), наконец (finally) order events.

english: In half a year he will return.
grammar: Утром, днём, вечером, ночью — instrumental case for parts of day.

english: They were told how to get there.
A spoken word cannot be taken back.
The broken chair needs to be fixed.
In summer we go to the dacha.
Usually I go to bed at eleven.
As a rule, he comes on time.
He said that he would come tomorrow.
He confirmed that the order is ready.
grammar: Tense does NOT shift in Russian reported speech like it does in English.

english: He reminded that tomorrow is a holiday.
He wrote that he is very busy.
grammar: Чтобы replaces imperative in reported speech: Он попросил, чтобы я пришёл.

english: He was told to come on Monday.
As she informed, the meeting is postponed.
He hinted that he wants a gift.
grammar: Ли introduces reported yes/no questions: Она спросила, приду ли я (She asked whether I'd come).

english: While reading a book, he drank tea.

target: Кровельщик заменил черепицу после сильного градобития.
english: The roofer replaced tiles after severe hailstorm.

target: В то же время она работала.
english: At the same time she was working.

target: Она убеждала, чтобы мы не волновались.
english: She was convincing us not to worry.

target: Он возразил, что это слишком дорого.
english: He objected that it is too expensive.
grammar: Прямая речь (direct speech) uses «»: Он сказал: «Я приду» = He said, 'I will come.'

target: В следующем году мы поедем в Италию.
english: Next year we will go to Italy.
grammar: В следующем году = next year (prepositional for 'in what year'). Поедем is perfective future — we will go (a planned trip).

english: The worried mother was waiting for a call.
grammar: Past active participle: stem + -вший/-ший: читавший (who read), пришедший (who came).

english: I haven't seen him for a long time.
grammar: Давно = 'for a long time' or 'long ago.' Не видел + genitive: не видел его = haven't seen him. Genitive after negated perception verbs.

english: A colleague reported that the project is ready.

target: Скоро спортсмен поёт песню на работе.
english: Soon the athlete sings a song at work.
grammar: Скоро (soon) + present tense for planned near-future. На работе = at work (prepositional for location).

target: Мама спросила, сделал ли я уроки.
english: Mom asked if I had done my homework.
grammar: Чтобы replaces imperative in reported speech: Он попросил, чтобы я пришёл.

target: Студент сказал, что не понял задание.
english: The student said he didn't understand the assignment.

target: Он убеждал, что это правильное решение.
english: He was convincing that it's the right decision.
grammar: Questions in reported speech use ли: Он спросил, придёт ли она.

target: Следующий автобус придёт через десять минут.
english: The next bus will come in ten minutes.

target: В то время мы жили в деревне.
english: At that time we lived in the village.
grammar: Утром, днём, вечером, ночью — instrumental case for parts of day.

target: Она сказала мне, что всё будет хорошо.
english: She told me that everything would be fine.
grammar: По словам (according to): По словам учителя (According to the teacher).

target: Письмо было отправлено по электронной почте вчера вечером.
english: The letter was sent by email yesterday evening.
grammar: Был + short participle for past passive: Письмо было написано = The letter was written.

target: Он объяснил, что опоздал из-за пробки.
english: He explained that he was late because of traffic.

target: Построенный дом выглядел красиво на фоне леса.
english: The built house looked beautiful against the forest backdrop.
grammar: Present passive participle: -емый/-имый: читаемый (being read), любимый (beloved).

target: Купленные вчера продукты уже лежали в холодильнике.
english: The groceries bought yesterday were already in the fridge.

target: Кружевница плела тонкие кружева на коклюшках при свече.
english: The lacemaker wove fine lace on bobbins by candlelight.

target: Обед был приготовлен из свежих продуктов с рынка.
english: Lunch was prepared from fresh produce from the market.
grammar: Embedded questions: Я не знаю, где он живёт. Russian keeps the comma before the question word.

target: В последний раз мы виделись в мае.
english: The last time we saw each other was in May.

target: Бегущая по улице собака напугала маленького ребёнка.
english: The dog running down the street scared the little child.

target: Сломанный стул отнесли в мастерскую для починки.
english: The broken chair was taken to the workshop for repair.

target: Деньги переведены на ваш счёт сегодня утром.
english: The money has been transferred to your account this morning.

target: Сыровар готовил пикантный горный сыр по традиционному рецепту.
english: The cheesemaker produced spicy mountain cheese by a traditional recipe.

target: Билеты на самолёт куплены, вылет в субботу утром.
english: Plane tickets have been bought, the flight is Saturday morning.
grammar: Participles agree with the noun in gender, number, and case like adjectives.

target: Новый мост через реку был открыт в июне.
english: The new bridge across the river was opened in June.
grammar: Семь пятниц на неделе (seven Fridays in a week) describes someone who changes their mind constantly.

target: Заказ будет доставлен к вам домой завтра утром.
english: The order will be delivered to your home tomorrow morning.

target: Сидящий на скамейке старик читает газету.

english: One and a half hours until departure.
Three men are waiting for the bus.
Four months of winter can be harsh.
Having watched the movie, we discussed it.
Thinking about the future, she was planning.
Two children are playing in the yard.
I need two hundred grams of butter.
grammar: Compound numbers: двадцать один (21) takes nominative, двадцать два (22) takes genitive singular.

target: Лёжа на диване, он смотрел телевизор.
english: Lying on the couch, he watched TV.
grammar: The gerund's subject must be the same as the main verb's subject.

target: Вернувшись из отпуска, мы начали работать.
english: Having returned from vacation, we started working.

target: Сосед слушал музыку на прошлой неделе.
english: The neighbor listened to music last week.
grammar: На прошлой неделе = last week. Слушал is past masculine imperfective of слушать — was listening/used to listen.

target: Не за что, обращайтесь в любое время.
english: Don't mention it, reach out any time.
grammar: Здравствуйте is formal; use Привет with friends.

target: Извините за беспокойство, не могли бы вы помочь?
english: Sorry for the trouble, could you help?
We need to buy a liter of milk.
Having written down the address, he went there.
It's a twenty minute walk to the market.

target: До встречи в понедельник, хороших выходных!
english: See you on Monday, have a nice weekend!
grammar: Как дела is casual; Как поживаете is more formal.

target: Бегая каждый день, он стал выносливее.
english: By running every day, he became more enduring.

target: Надев пальто, он вышел на улицу.
english: Having put on a coat, he went outside.
grammar: Formal address uses first name + patronymic: Иван Петрович, Мария Ивановна.

target: Постирав одежду, он повесил её сушиться.
english: Having washed clothes, he hung them to dry.

target: Приготовив подарки, мы поехали на праздник.
english: Having prepared gifts, we went to the celebration.

target: Ваше мнение очень ценно для нас.
english: Your (formal) opinion is very valuable to us.
grammar: Ты is informal (friends, family); Вы is formal (strangers, elders, professional).

target: Информация обновляется на сайте каждый час.
english: Information is updated on the website every hour.

target: Магазин открыт с девяти до шести.
english: The store is open from nine to six.
The speed is one hundred kilometers per hour.
The twenty-first century is the century of technology.

target: Подготовившись к экзамену, она чувствовала себя уверенно.
english: Having prepared for the exam, she felt confident.
grammar: The switch from Вы to ты (тыканье) is usually proposed by the older or higher-status person.

target: Ужин был приготовлен мамой из свежих продуктов.
english: Dinner was prepared by mom from fresh ingredients.

target: Статья была переведена на пять языков мира.
english: The article was translated into five world languages.

target: Результаты экзамена будут объявлены на следующей неделе.
english: The exam results will be announced next week.

target: Ошибка была замечена и исправлена до публикации.
english: The mistake was noticed and corrected before publication.
grammar: Passive agent uses instrumental case: Книга написана Толстым = The book was written by Tolstoy.

english: Having solved the problem, the student raised his hand.
Having turned off the TV, he went to bed.
grammar: Gerunds don't change form — they are invariable verbal adverbs.

english: Having dialed the number, she waited for an answer.
grammar: The gerund's subject must be the same as the main verb's subject.

english: One man is not a warrior in the field.

target: Взяв зонт, она пошла на прогулку.
english: Having taken an umbrella, she went for a walk.

target: Новый закон был принят парламентом в прошлом месяце.
english: The new law was adopted by parliament last month.

target: Уроки проводятся каждый день кроме субботы и воскресенья.
english: Classes are held every day except Saturday and Sunday.
grammar: Был + short participle for past passive: Письмо было написано = The letter was written.

target: Подарки были куплены заранее для всех членов семьи.
english: Gifts were bought in advance for all family members.

target: Написав письмо, она пошла на почту.
english: Having written the letter, she went to the post office.

target: Положив вещи, она села на диван.
english: Having put down her things, she sat on the couch.

target: Урожай собирается осенью после первых заморозков.
english: The harvest is gathered in autumn after the first frosts.

target: Пациент был осмотрен врачом и отправлен домой.
english: The patient was examined by the doctor and sent home.
grammar: Был + short participle for past passive: Письмо было написано = The letter was written.

target: Мусор убирается с улиц каждое утро дворниками.
english: Garbage is cleaned from the streets every morning by janitors.

target: Братан, одолжи мне телефон на пару минут.
english: Bro, lend me your phone for a couple of minutes.
grammar: Formal greeting: Здравствуйте. Informal: Привет.

target: Обед был подан вовремя, все гости остались довольны.
english: Lunch was served on time, all the guests were satisfied.
grammar: Passive with -ся: Дом строится = The house is being built. Книга читается = The book is being read.

target: Хочешь чаю с мёдом, я только что заварил свежий?
english: Want some tea with honey, I just brewed some fresh?

target: Аварийное здание сносится по решению городских властей.
english: The emergency building is being demolished by decision of city authorities.

target: Собрание проводится каждую среду в десять утра.
english: The meeting is held every Wednesday at ten in the morning.
grammar: Проводиться = to be held (passive -ся). Каждую среду = every Wednesday (accusative for recurring days). В десять утра = at 10 AM.

target: Новый мировой рекорд установлен на соревнованиях в Москве.
english: A new world record was set at the competition in Moscow.

target: Хорошего вечера и приятного отдыха после трудного дня!
english: Have a good evening and pleasant rest after a hard day!

target: Новый мост будет построен через эту реку к лету.
english: A new bridge will be built across this river by summer.
grammar: Passive with -ся: Дом строится = The house is being built. Книга читается = The book is being read.

target: Путь на поезде из Москвы во Владивосток занимает примерно семь дней.
english: The train journey from Moscow to Vladivostok takes approximately seven days.

target: Включив свет, она увидела кота на столе.
english: Having turned on the light, she saw a cat on the table.

target: Праздник отмечается каждый год в первый день лета.
english: The holiday is celebrated every year on the first day of summer.
grammar: Past passive participles end in -нный/-тый: прочитанный (that was read), открытый (opened).

target: В квартире пять комнат и большой балкон с видом на реку.
english: The apartment has five rooms and a large balcony overlooking the river.
grammar: Ordinal numbers agree in gender: первый (m), первая (f), первое (n).

target: Машина ремонтируется в автосервисе уже вторую неделю.
english: The car has been repaired at the auto service for the second week.

target: Границы заповедника чётко определены на карте местности.
english: The boundaries of the nature reserve are clearly defined on the area map.
grammar: Был + short participle for past passive: Письмо было написано = The letter was written.

target: Позолотчик покрывал раму зеркала тонким слоем сусального золота.
english: The gilder covered the mirror frame with a thin layer of gold leaf.

target: Позвольте откланяться, мне нужно успеть на вечерний поезд.
english: Allow me to take my leave, I need to catch the evening train.
grammar: Formal greeting: Здравствуйте. Informal: Привет.

target: Каждую весну вдоль главных дорог города высаживают новые деревья.
english: New trees are planted every spring along the main roads of the city.
grammar: Short passive participles: Книга прочитана (read), Дом построен (built), Окно открыто (opened).

target: Рисуя пейзажи в парке, он чувствовал полное спокойствие и умиротворение.
english: While drawing landscapes in the park, he felt completely relaxed and at peace.

target: Закон нарушен водителем, превысившим скорость на трассе.
english: The law was broken by the driver who exceeded the speed on the highway.

target: Задача была решена студентами за полчаса на экзамене.
english: The problem was solved by the students in half an hour on the exam.
grammar: Был + short participle for past passive: Письмо было написано = The letter was written.

target: У нас дома три кошки, и у каждой свой уникальный характер.
english: We have three cats at home and each one has its own unique personality.

target: Как ты себя сегодня чувствуешь, всё ещё устал после вчерашней долгой дороги?
english: How do you feel today, are you still tired after the long journey yesterday?

target: У неё два младших брата, которые оба ходят в одну школу в нашем районе.
english: She has two younger brothers who both attend the same school in our district.

target: Мост через реку был построен в тысяча восемьсот девяносто пятом году и используется до сих пор.
english: The bridge across the river was built in eighteen ninety-five and is still used today.

target: Он живёт в этом городе пятнадцать лет и знает каждую улицу наизусть.
english: He has been living in this city for fifteen years and knows every street by heart.
grammar: Compound numbers: двадцать один (21) takes nominative, двадцать два (22) takes genitive singular.

target: Ответь, когда сможешь, спешки нет, но мне нужно твоё мнение по этому вопросу.
english: Please answer when you can, there is no hurry but I need your opinion on this.
Both sisters work.
We waited twenty minutes.
